newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Moslems mourn war dead on Islamic holiday.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Moslems mourn war dead on Islamic holiday.

text.p: Moslems in Sarajevo prayed at ancient mosques and mourned those killed during the Bosnian war on Sunday when they celebrated the Islamic holiday of Bairam.
The Moslem chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, joined fellow worshippers at the 16th century Begova mosque on a crisp winter morning.

Sunday newspapers published greetings from Izetbegovic and the country's Islamic senior cleric, Reis Ul-Ulema Mustafa Ceric, who said there were signs peace was taking root more than a year after fighting ended in the former Yugoslav republic.
"We do have reason to feel joy because Bosnian wounds are healing, refugees are returning to their homes, peace and freedom is coming to Bosnia," Ceric said in a statement.
"For all these good things we are indebted to those who gave their lives."
Moslems mourn the dead on the second day of Bairam, a three- day holiday which follows a month of daytime fast and prayer.
Ceric said Moslems would not be fully content until all refugees returned to their homes, war criminals faced justice and Bosnians were allowed free movement across the country.
After 3-1/2 years of war which displaced hundreds of thousands of people, Sarajevo is a predominantly Moslem city with small Serb and Croat minorities.
Celebratory gunfire echoed across the capital after religious services ended, marking the beginning of three days of feasting and parties.
